industries.name: E-commerce and online marketplaces
industries.how_to_spot: Receipts from AMAZON PAYMENTS, SHOPIFY, PAYPAL, STRIPE, EBAY, ETSY, TIKTOK; platform fee lines; many small receipts

industries.name: Property - trading and development
industries.how_to_spot: Large property purchase / sale receipts; completion statements; SDLT; builders' invoices; development loans

industries.name: Property - letting (investment)
industries.how_to_spot: Rent received; letting agent receipts; mortgage payments; tenancy deposits

industries.name: Construction and trades (CIS)
industries.how_to_spot: Receipts at 80% / 70% of invoices; CIS in descriptions; subcontractor payments with no VAT; reverse charge invoices

industries.name: Restaurants, takeaways and cafes
industries.how_to_spot: Card terminal settlements (Dojo, SumUp, Worldpay, Square); Uber Eats, Deliveroo, Just Eat payouts; cash bankings; food suppliers

industries.name: Retail shops and wholesale
industries.how_to_spot: EPOS takings; card settlements; wholesaler purchases; mixed VAT rates

industries.name: Hair, beauty and barbers
industries.how_to_spot: Card terminal settlements; chair or room rental receipts; product purchases; payments to stylists

industries.name: Contractors and consultants (IT, locums, one-person companies)
industries.how_to_spot: Few customers; agency remittances; regular director dividends; home and mileage claims

industries.name: Healthcare and care (medical, dental, care homes, pharmacy)
industries.how_to_spot: NHS / CCG / council receipts; NHS BSA payments (pharmacy); agency staff; CQC fees

industries.name: Solicitors and professional firms
industries.how_to_spot: Client bank account; disbursements; SRA / practising certificate fees; WIP

industries.name: Recruitment and staffing
industries.how_to_spot: Large payroll for temps; invoice finance / factoring receipts; umbrella company payments

industries.name: Transport and haulage
industries.how_to_spot: Fuel cards; HGV hire purchase; tolls and congestion charges; subcontract hauliers

industries.name: Digital agencies, software and SaaS
industries.how_to_spot: Stripe / subscription receipts; annual licences sold in advance; developer salaries; contractor payments abroad

industries.name: Manufacturing
industries.how_to_spot: Raw material purchases; production wages; machinery; finished goods sales

industries.name: Charities and churches (charitable companies)
industries.how_to_spot: Donations; Gift Aid receipts; grants; restricted funds

industries.name: Holding and investment companies
industries.how_to_spot: Dividends from subsidiaries; intercompany transfers; broker statements

rules.rule: Settlement / payout reports per platform for the full year
rules.action: Add to Notes & Queries if not uploaded

Year-end stock report incl. stock at Amazon FBA / 3PL
Purchase invoices, import documents, postponed VAT accounting (CDS) statements
One clearing account per platform, treated like a bank
Sales grossed up: payout + fees + refunds + reserve held = gross sales
Platform fees and advertising to selling costs, never netted off sales
Import VAT under postponed accounting through boxes 1 and 4; duty and freight to cost of sales
Opening held + gross sales - fees - refunds - payouts = closing per platform report
Payouts matched to bank receipts line by line
Gross sales per platform report = GL sales by platform
Sales equal to payouts (posted net)
Fees below the firm's % of sales; refunds above the firm's %
No closing stock for a goods seller
Overseas seller: marketplace may account for the VAT
Completion statements for every purchase and sale
List of properties held at year end with costs to date and expected sale price
Development loan statements; builders' invoices
Purchase price, SDLT, legal fees, improvements and development costs to stock / WIP of that property
Sale proceeds to turnover; that property's cost to cost of sales
Loan interest: expense, or added to WIP if that is the firm's policy
Property schedule: one row per property - address, date bought, costs, sold, closing stock
Closing stock at the lower of cost and net realisable value
Property costs in the P&L of a trading company
Sale with no completion statement
Trading v letting not confirmed
Letting agent statements for the full year
Mortgage statements; completion statements; works invoices
Tenancy deposit details
Purchase price, SDLT, legal fees and improvements capitalised to that property
Repairs and maintenance to the P&L
Agent statements grossed up: gross rent to income; commission, repairs and fees to expenses; net to bank
Rent held by the agent at year end = debtor
Tenant deposit held by the company = liability, not income
FRS 102: fair value, no depreciation, deferred tax on the gain. FRS 105: cost
Gross rent per agent statements = rent in GL; net per statements = bank receipts from agent
Each mortgage agrees to the lender statement
Rent received equal to bank receipts (posted net)
Improvements expensed
Commercial property with VAT charged and no option to tax on file
CIS payment and deduction statements from every contractor
Contractor clients: CIS300 returns, subcontractor verification
EPS showing CIS suffered set against PAYE
Sales grossed up: net receipt + CIS deducted = invoice
CIS suffered to a CIS debtor, never to expenses
Contractor: CIS withheld to a CIS liability, paid with PAYE
VAT domestic reverse charge on construction services between VAT/CIS-registered businesses
CIS suffered per statements = CIS debtor movement; set-off per EPS; balance = repayment claim
Contractor: deductions per CIS300 = liability paid
Sales equal to bank receipts (posted net of CIS)
Reverse-charge invoices carrying UK VAT, or VAT missing to end users
Retentions not in debtors; long contracts with no WIP
Vans and tools: capital allowances (AIA) - not cars
EPOS Z-reports (daily takings by payment type)
Card terminal and delivery platform statements
Cash banking records; stock count; tips / tronc records
Card and delivery sales grossed up; fees and commission posted separately
Cash takings recorded in full, not only what was banked
Hot food and takeaway hot food standard-rated; cold takeaway food may be zero-rated
Takings per Z-reports = sales in GL
Card / delivery sales per reports = settlements + fees
Cash takings - banked - cash expenses = cash in hand
Gross margin far from last year
No cash sales in a cash trade; negative cash
Delivery platform sales posted net
EPOS reports by VAT rate; stock count at year end
VAT retail scheme used (if any)
Sales split by VAT rate (standard, zero, exempt) as per the retail scheme
Card settlements grossed up for fees
Takings per EPOS = sales in GL; stock per count = D1
Gross margin movement v last year
Stock not counted or same as last year
Booking system / till reports; chair rental agreements
Chair / room rental income is standard-rated for VAT
Product sales and services coded separately
Stylists paid as self-employed v employees
Takings per till / booking reports = sales in GL
Regular payments to individuals with no payroll
Tips not recorded or not through payroll
Agency remittances or self-billing statements; timesheets for unbilled days
Contracts (for the IR35 question)
Income per remittance gross; unbilled days at year end as accrued income
Use of home and mileage
VAT flat rate % and limited cost trader test
IR35 status not confirmed
Personal costs in the P&L
NHS / council remittances; pharmacy NHSBSA statements; payroll and agency invoices
Medical care by registered health professionals and welfare services by registered providers are generally VAT exempt
Pharmacy: dispensed NHS prescriptions zero-rated; retail sales at their own rates
Income accrued for months paid in arrears by NHS / council
Income per remittances = sales in GL
Pharmacy stock per count = D1
VAT claimed on costs relating to exempt income (partial exemption)
Large agency staff costs with no contracts
Office and client bank statements; client ledger balances; WIP report
Client money is not the firm's money: client bank and client ledger kept off the firm's P&L
Disbursements v recharges: recharges carry VAT, true disbursements do not
Unbilled work at year end as accrued income (WIP)
Client bank = total client ledger balances
Client money posted to sales
Professional indemnity insurance prepayment
Payroll for temps; timesheets for the last week; invoice finance statements
Unbilled timesheets at year end as accrued income, with the related wage cost
Invoice finance account treated as a loan or bank control, not netted against debtors
Holiday pay accrual for temps
Invoice finance balance agrees to the finance company statement
Margin per placement far from last year
Fuel card statements; HP agreements; vehicle list
HGVs and vans on HP: asset per vehicle, loan per agreement
Capital allowances: lorries and vans are not cars (AIA available)
International freight may be zero-rated - check VAT on cross-border jobs
Fuel per fuel card statements = fuel in GL
Fines and penalties in the P&L
Subscription / billing report; contracts with retainers
Income billed in advance for future months to deferred income
Overseas services bought in: reverse charge VAT
Development costs expensed unless the firm's policy capitalises them
Deferred income per billing report = G balance
R&D activity: query if a claim is intended (merged scheme / ERIS rules apply)
Stock count split raw materials, WIP and finished goods; costing basis
Stock includes production overheads, at the lower of cost and net realisable value
Machinery: full expensing / AIA
Stock per count = D1; movement through cost of sales
Gross margin movement; slow-moving stock
Donation records, Gift Aid claims, grant agreements, trustee minutes
Funds split restricted / unrestricted / endowment (Charities SORP)
Gift Aid claimed but not received at year end as a debtor
Grants with conditions not yet met: deferred
Each fund: b/f + income - spend = c/f
Trustee payments or expenses
Accounts format must follow the SORP, not FRS 105
Subsidiaries' accounts; dividend vouchers; broker / investment statements; intercompany confirmations
Dividends received to dividend income (usually not taxable)
Intercompany balances by company, never netted
Each intercompany balance agrees to the other company's books
Investments agree to statements
Associated companies not set in H1 (CT rate)
